title: Positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s): near-criticality and uniqueness
description:
Paper (48 pages) with its LaTeX sources and ancillary files (certificate scripts, parameter files and logs), a Lean 4 formalisation of the paper's logical spine with its axiom ledger, and a companion manuscript and three notes from the same project. Preprint, October 2026; not yet peer-reviewed.

We study the positive solutions of Weil's explicit formula with the archimedean data of the Riemann zeta function: pairs of positive measures, one on the zero side and one on the prime side beyond log 2/(2π). By linear-programming duality such pairs exist if and only if a positivity statement involving neither zeros nor primes holds; its slack κ* gives the optimal degree-one explicit-formula conductor bound qmin = exp(−2πκ*). We conjecture that ζ's own pair is the only solution; this does not imply the Riemann hypothesis, but makes it equivalent to existence. We prove it when the zero measure lives on the zeros of ζ and the origin, whatever the prime measure, and when it lives on the zeros plus countably many summable points with the prime measure on the Bondarenko–Radchenko–Seip nodes. Certificates of the form Ξ2(H + ε·exp(−πt2)), with H ≥ 1 a polynomial in t2, vanish at every zero of ζ and show unconditionally that κ* ≤ 1.1508391·10−906 and that every solution has ∫Ξ2 dμ ≤ 3.21·10−906. Uniqueness would follow from asymptotic properties of such functions defined by Hermite interpolation at the prime powers.

The Lean 4 formalisation (paper/anc/lean) states the headline results (Theorems A–D and the magic-function corollary) faithfully in Lean and proves them from Mathlib plus an explicit axiom ledger of 23 axioms (cited classical theorems, analytic steps proved in the paper but not yet formalised, and computer-assisted certificates); it contains no sorry, and its build and audit run in continuous integration.

Two theorems and their proofs, the zero-side support theorem (Theorem 3.6) and the extension of Theorem B from finitely to countably many extra zeros (Theorem 3.8), together with their consequences, were contributed by OpenAI's Astra during an independent review of an earlier version of the paper, and were then checked line by line by independent Claude referees. The rest of the mathematics, proofs and text was produced by AI agents (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5) under the author's direction; see the paper's AI-use statement.
